subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — next steps

Thanks for the time today, Sarah — great discussion on production targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the first pass benchmarks:

Summary (from call)
- Target throughput: 100 QPS sustained for the primary inference path (text generation).
- Concurrency target: 20 concurrent sessions with per-session streaming.
- Latency SLOs: first-token latency < 100ms (p50), p95 end-to-end response latency < 300ms, p99 < 600ms.
- Streaming: client expects chunked token streaming; first-byte latency is critical for UX.
- Failure behaviour: fallback to smaller model acceptable for non-critical paths; must surface precise error codes for retries.

What we need from EdgeFin to run a reproducible benchmark
1) Confirm representative prompt / payload distribution (you mentioned 60% short prompts, 30% medium, 10% long).
2) Any session affinity or sticky-key requirements for KV cache behaviour.
3) Example request payloads and auth headers (we can scrub private data).

Deliverables from Redwood
- Benchmark harness (attached): redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz — includes load generator, measurement scripts, and a reproducibility README.
- Prompt set: edgefin-prompt-set-v2.csv (attached) with tokenized lengths and expected behaviors.
- Measurement definitions doc (summary below) and a public Drive link.

Measurement defs (short)
- First-token latency: time from request accept to delivery of first token to client socket.
- Total-response latency: time from request accept to final token delivered.
- Token throughput: tokens/sec per instance and aggregated.
- Tail percentiles: report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both first-token and total-response.
- Reproducibility: run with fixed model version, seed where available, and recorded model config (batch size, kv cache state).

Next steps
- Sarah: confirm prompt distribution and share any sample payloads by EOD Tue 5/11.
- Marcus/Dev: review the harness README and call out any infra constraints for streaming (timeouts, connection limits).
- Redwood: run smoke benchmark on our staging infra once we get samples, share raw logs and aggregated metrics.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.tar.gz (scripts + README), edgefin-prompt-set-v2.csv

Thanks — Marissa
--

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Prompt distribution: confirmed (60/30/10). I attached a sanitized sample set (we'll upload the full set to a shared Drive link by EOD).
- For streaming, our client expects a first token within ~120ms at p50; p95 should be under 300ms — your targets look aligned, but p99 for longer completions can be up to 700ms.
- Concurrency: the 20 concurrent sessions is a good initial target; we may scale to 40 for peak windows.
- Sticky sessions: yes — we rely on session affinity for per-session KV cache to stay warm on session continuation, but the cache can be cold for new sessions.

Action items from EdgeFin
- We'll upload the full prompt set and a sanitized traffic trace to the Drive folder referenced below.
- Infra will share current timeout settings (we have aggressive 60s timeouts on the LB; we'll check if chunk-level timeouts exist).

One concern: during demo we saw a small number of aborted streams under bursty load — we want the harness to capture both successful and aborted traces so we can correlate with LB logs.

Link to sample artifacts (will add full set shortly): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeFinBenchmark

Thanks — Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — measurement defs

Following up with more detail on measurement definitions and reproducibility so both teams measure the same things:

Measurement details
- Time origin: t0 = server accept (HTTP 202) timestamp. We will capture both client-side and server-side clocks and align via NTP offset.
- First-token latency: measured at ingress proxy (time to first byte on the response stream). If client chunking introduces buffering, we'll note client-side seen-first-byte separately.
- Total-response latency: ingress accept -> last token out. For streaming long completions, we'll also report time-to-last-byte and tokens/sec across the stream.
- Concurrency semantics: emulate 'sessions' in the harness — each session will maintain socket open and do multiple prompt/response cycles to exercise KV cache warm/cold starts.
- Load profile: 10-minute ramps to steady-state, a 5-minute burst window, then a 10-minute cooldown. We'll run at three target QPS levels: 50, 100, 150 to map scaling.
- Statistical reporting: include p50/p90/p95/p99 and sample counts; include error breakdowns by HTTP status and stream abort codes.

Reproducibility
- Record: model name/version, quantization profile, seed (if model supports deterministic sampling), batch sizes, runtime config (batching window, max batch size), hardware (GPU type, driver/kernel), and commit id of the harness.
- Store raw traces (request/response timestamps and headers) in the Drive folder and provide a short script to re-run aggregated metrics from raw traces.

We will attach a small harness tarball with the measurement scripts — Marissa attached a first pass; I've added a reproducibility checklist inside the README.

Marcus
